phases: Rule-based fraud detection is generating more noise than signal.
Recovery cost for flagged-but-legitimate transactions ≈ 4× the value of the actual fraud.
Fraud analysts: need fewer, higher-confidence alerts.
Compliance & risk: explainability, auditability, zero tolerance for false negatives.
Leadership: cost reduction without added risk exposure.
Vision: reduce friction for legitimate users while improving fraud signal precision.
Partner with data science on where AI adds real value — and where rules already suffice.
Sequence an MVP that assists analysts rather than replacing their decisions.
Design an 8-agent architecture: orchestration, inter-agent data contracts, retrieval, tool interfaces, prompt governance.
Build a rubric-based evaluation harness from human-reviewed SOPs.
Turn production misses into prompt and logic improvements.
Earn analyst trust before expanding autonomy.
Scale automation to roughly 60% of manual operations.
30% fewer false positives · 28% better detection accuracy
50% operational efficiency gain · ~$1M indirect expense losses prevented

lens.customer: Customer lens → cut the false declines that hit legitimate customers first.
